unit.title: Multiplication and Division
unit.blurb: Multiplying 3-digit numbers by 1-digit numbers and 2-digit by 2-digit numbers, dividing with remainders, and tests of divisibility by 2, 4, 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Estimate and multiply whole numbers up to 1000 by 1-digit numbers, and 2-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers.

O2.t: Estimate and divide whole numbers up to 1000 by 1-digit numbers, and decide what to do with remainders.

O3.t: Use tests of divisibility by 2, 4, 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100.

p: Divide using known facts: 96 ÷ 4 → 80 ÷ 4 = 20 and 16 ÷ 4 = 4, so **24**.
A **remainder** is what is left over. 50 ÷ 6 = 8 r2. In a problem, decide whether to round up or down.

lesson.t: Why remainders can be rounded up or down
p: In a story problem, the remainder means something. 26 children in cars of 4 needs 7 cars (round up), but 26 sweets in bags of 4 makes only 6 full bags (round down).

p: **÷ 2**: the last digit is even. **÷ 5**: ends in 0 or 5. **÷ 10**: ends in 0. **÷ 100**: ends in 00.
**÷ 4**: the last two digits make a multiple of 4. **÷ 25**: ends in 00, 25, 50 or 75. **÷ 50**: ends in 00 or 50.

lesson.t: Why the tests for 3 and 9 use digit sums
p: 10 is one more than 9, so each ten leaves 1 extra when divided by 3 or 9. Adding the digits counts those extras.
By 3: digit sum divisible by 3.
By 9: digit sum divisible by 9.
By 4: last two digits divisible by 4.
34 is even but not divisible by 4: 34 is not a multiple of 4.
